title: Rabbi Yudan bar Guriya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Sheviit, chapter 2, near the end of halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.2.3.5), Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba says: “Rabbi Yudan bar Guriya waters with a basket and hoes.”[^1] Perhaps he is Rabbi Yudan Giriya mentioned in [Taanit, chapter 3, halakhah 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.3.9.4), who said: “This Choni the Circle-Drawer was the grandson of Choni the Circle-Drawer.” Seder HaDorot reads R' Yudan Meriya, while the entry R' Yehudah ben Pedaya reads R' Yudan Gidya.[^2]

notes.text: The exact Guggenheimer Sheviit passage names Rabbi Chiyya bar Ba as the reporter and Rabbi Yudan bar Guriya as the subject. This supports expanding אר״ח בר אבא as Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, rather than Chaggai, and keeps the patronymic with the reporter. [Penei Moshe on that passage](https://www.sefaria.org/Penei_Moshe_on_Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.2.3.5.3), in the Piotrków 1898–1900 edition, explains בסלא as בסל, “with a basket,” a different watering method used in the sabbatical year. Its next comment explains ועדר as hoeing. The earlier vegetable-field and flock renderings are withdrawn. Hyman’s locator פ״ב סה״ג is read as chapter 2, near the end of halakhah 3; the exact passage has now been checked, rather than assigning a subdivision from an abbreviation alone.

The fetched Taanit passage explicitly names Rabbi Yudan Giriya and says that this Choni was the grandson of Choni; no intervening ancestor is added. Hyman’s tentative “perhaps” and the Guriya/Giriya/Meriya/Gidya name variants remain distinct. Seder HaDorot and its quoted name variants have not been independently checked, so their abbreviated titles remain neutral R', as does the cross-reference to R' Yehudah ben Pedaya. סה״ד is rendered by the customary title Seder HaDorot; it is not a claim to have verified that work’s text. The unstated subject of גורס is left neutral as “the entry … reads.” These source correspondences do not establish an identity between the figures.
